verdicts.what_goes_wrong: capture_output=True overwrites a caller stdout/stderr and Popen has no input=, unlike subprocess.run.
verdicts.evidence: codegraph.py:105-121 docstring 'subprocess.run for a CodeGraph command'; all callers (lines 430,452,519,868,1651) pass only stdin=DEVNULL, capture_output, text, timeout, check; none passes stdout/stderr/input.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: For a pin that fails in a non-default registry, the hint tells the user to run `models sync --apply` and `models set` with no --registry-path, so they change the default registry.
verdicts.evidence: unroutable_pin_hint(source, registry, *, adapter) has no registry_path (registry_sync.py:182); resolve_and_bind_explicit_pin has `path` from payload registry_path (routing_authority.py:92) but _pin_failure_detail (line 23) does not pass it; SYNC_COMMAND and enable_command are fixed strings; `models sync` has --registry-path (_parser.py:2676).

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A pin whose starter model exists under a different id (disabled) is reported as absent and the user is told to run `models sync --apply`, which skips it, so the repair does nothing.
verdicts.evidence: Probed: registry with claude-code/my-haiku disabled, hint returns 'is a starter registry entry that this registry does not have ... --apply'; plan_starter_sync (registry_sync.py:115-118) puts it in covered; test_same_model_below_a_different_id_is_not_added.

registry_sync.py:82 `if not spec.is_routable or ...: return spec` keeps a starter entry's own disabled state and reason; no starter spec is non-routable today (probed 0 of starter_registry()); docs only promise enabled=false, and a disabled entry already satisfies that.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: The enable command text is duplicated in the CLI, so it can drift from enable_command, but today the output is the same text.
verdicts.evidence: commands_models.py:741-744 'puppetmaster models set <id> enabled=true disabled_reason= disabled_authority=' vs registry_sync.py:74-78 enable_command; the CLI text keeps the <id> placeholder, so it is a template and not a wrong result.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: input= passed to _run_cli reaches Popen and raises TypeError instead of feeding stdin.
verdicts.evidence: codegraph.py:105-121 passes **kwargs to subprocess.Popen; no caller of _run_cli passes input=.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A renamed file whose source name contains ' -> ' (git quotes the source) gives a wrong path fragment, so the freshness sample lists a bogus path.
verdicts.evidence: _porcelain_path (codegraph.py:1716-1727) does rest.split(' -> ', 1)[1] before it looks at quotes, though its docstring says 'dest on rename'; _git_changes_since line 1752 feeds it every `git status --porcelain` line. The drift is still counted, so the harm is only a wrong sample name. Not run against git here (command was blocked); derived from the code.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: Same fault as claim 3: a disabled starter model under a custom id is reported as absent and the sync repair skips it.
verdicts.evidence: Probed with disabled claude-code/my-haiku: hint says the registry does not have claude-code/haiku-5-5; plan_starter_sync covered branch at registry_sync.py:115-118.

docs/MODEL_ROUTING.md:241 'doctor gives the warning registry-starter-sync with the count of absent ids'; the same doc says sync adds locked-adapter entries with enabled false; diagnostics.py:208 counts plan.additions, which includes locked adapters by design (registry_sync.py:119-127).

puppetmaster/model_registry.py:1823-1851 docstring: 'Accepts both cursor/grok-4-5 and grok-4.5 (and slug-equivalent forms ...)'; the last-segment token match is the designed fallback, it is limited to enabled entries of the given adapter, and more than one match raises AmbiguousModelPinError.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: enable_command does not quote the id, so an id with a space or shell metacharacter would give a broken command.
verdicts.evidence: registry_sync.py:74-78 has no quoting, but both callers pass only starter ids: registry_sync.py:90 (spec.id from starter_registry) and registry_sync.py:210 (present.id equals starter_pin.registry_id, found by starter id); starter ids hold no spaces or metacharacters.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: `models sync --apply` on a registry file that cannot be read or written raises OSError/PermissionError (load_registry read_text, write_private_text) and the user gets a traceback, not `error:` and exit 1.
verdicts.evidence: commands_models.py:674-678 catches only RuntimeError; model_registry.py:243-245 catches only JSONDecodeError around read_text; registry_sync.py write_private_text writes the file.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: After a BaseException (such as KeyboardInterrupt) in communicate, the child is killed but not waited and its pipes are not closed until GC, unlike subprocess.run.
verdicts.evidence: codegraph.py:129-131 kills the tree and re-raises with no process.wait() or pipe close; only an interrupt can reach it, the timeout path calls communicate again (codegraph.py:125), and the Popen finalizer reaps the child later, so no product caller sees a wrong result.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: `models set <id> effort=<level>` on claude-code or codex replaces the whole extra_args list, so any other extra_args flags in the entry are silently removed.
verdicts.evidence: payload_defaults = {**(spec.payload_defaults or {}), **effort_defaults} is a shallow merge, and model_payload_defaults_for_effort returns {'extra_args': [...]} (lines 93, 116); the comment at lines 173-174 says unrelated defaults survive.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A malformed mcp.json gives the detail 'no puppetmaster stdio entry in mcp.json' instead of 'mcp.json unreadable', so with the omp CLI present the warn text names the wrong cause (and with no CLI the check is optional, not warn).
verdicts.evidence: diagnostics.py omp_pilot_check: the except branch sets mcp_detail='mcp.json unreadable: ...' and mcp={}; the following else branch (entry missing) overwrites it with 'no puppetmaster stdio entry in mcp.json'.

registry_sync.py sync_starter_registry docstring: 'The write appends rows to the parsed JSON document. It does not rebuild the rows that are already there, so their fields, their key order and the fields this release does not know stay as they are.' Both reads run under InterProcessFileLock, so the views cannot drift; this is a style point, not a wrong result.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: When the project folder or a rule path is a string-prefix sibling of HOME (HOME /home/bob, project /home/bob2/proj), relative_to raises ValueError and the doctor reports an existing valid rule file as an error row.
verdicts.evidence: diagnostics.py:454-457: str(p).startswith(str(Path.home())) then p.relative_to(Path.home()); root comes from run_doctor (line 75) and is the user's working folder.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A pin that matches a disabled entry stored under a custom id gets the hint that the starter entry is absent and to run `models sync`, but sync skips it as covered by that custom id, so the advice does not help.
verdicts.evidence: registry_sync.py unroutable_pin_hint looks up the registry only by starter_pin.registry_id; plan_starter_sync puts an entry with the same execution identity in `covered` and does not add it.

CHANGELOG v1.51.1 scopes the fix to 'The five callers in puppetmaster/codegraph.py' and to the npm shim that starts the real Node binary; codegraph_repair.py:439 docstring says it deliberately runs the JS entry point through the same Node binary, not the shim, so subprocess.run kills the direct node child and no shim child exists.

Ran a check: registry entry agentic/openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna-pro; resolve_and_bind_explicit_pin gave model=gpt-5.6-luna and pinned_adapter_model_name=gpt-5.6-luna; validate_pinned_dispatch(payload, adapter='agentic') returned OK with no error (routing_authority.py:151-162, worker_runtime.py:108).

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: When the registry holds the same adapter and model under a different id, a failed pin tells the user to run `models sync --apply`, which skips the entry (covered) and adds nothing, so the advice does not fix the pin.
verdicts.evidence: registry_sync.py:195 looks up the entry with spec.id == starter_pin.registry_id only; CHANGELOG v1.51.0: 'A starter entry is not added when the registry has the same adapter and model below a different id.'

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A task text exactly equal to a flag token such as '--format' is dropped with the next argument.
verdicts.evidence: codegraph.py:717-750 scans all argv after 'context'; codegraph.py:503 puts the task at index 1, but no product caller produces a task that is exactly --format, --max-nodes or --max-files (the task is worker goal text).

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A registry file that is not UTF-8 (for example UTF-16 from PowerShell redirection) makes load_registry raise UnicodeDecodeError, which is not caught, so doctor shows an 'error' check 'check raised: UnicodeDecodeError' instead of the 'registry unreadable' warning.
verdicts.evidence: diagnostics.py:199-201 catches only RuntimeError; model_registry.py:243-246 catches only json.JSONDecodeError around read_text(encoding='utf-8'); _guard (diagnostics.py:42-45) turns it into an error Check, so doctor does not crash.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: PUPPETMASTER_CODEGRAPH_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=inf raises OverflowError (not ValueError) out of a function documented as never raising.
verdicts.evidence: codegraph.py:374-381 catches ValueError only; ensure_codegraph_provisioned docstring says 'fully best-effort ... rather than raising'; the variable is a number of seconds (default 300) and no product code sets it to inf.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: The test could fail on a slow runner if the child needs more than 3 s to write its pid file, although _run_cli is correct.
verdicts.evidence: tests/test_codegraph_process_group.py:51 timeout=3 and line 53 assertTrue(pid_file.exists(), ...); the owner must decide whether a 3 s margin is acceptable on slow CI (Windows, coverage) or must grow.

registry_sync.py:157-161 and CHANGELOG v1.51.0 promise only that rows keep 'fields, key order, position and unknown fields' (a json round trip keeps all; \u00e8 and 1.5 are the same values); _plan_for_path calls load_registry (model_registry.py:231, 'atomically validate') under the lock before the write, and the appended rows come from the starter registry.

verdicts.what_goes_wrong: A changed file with a non-ASCII or special-character name is quoted by git, the path is not decoded, stat fails, and the file is counted as drift even when the index is newer, so the index shows as stale.
verdicts.evidence: _run_git (codegraph.py:1643) passes no core.quotepath=false; _porcelain_path (codegraph.py:1716-1727) only strips the outer quotes; _git_changes_since treats an OSError from stat as changed (mtime = cutoff + 1).
